account-and-settings.reason: Arc’s `LoginCentered` props expose its own passkey/email-code/SSO flow and `onSignIn`, with no caller-rendered Clerk slot. Sign-in and sign-up use the actual Clerk `<SignIn>` / `<SignUp>` components with route-safe redirect props. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/blocks/login-centered.

This is an email/password/provider signup engine with name/password-strength/opt-in/completion fields, not a render shell for Clerk. Its callbacks can connect a custom auth API, but the current presenter needs Clerk’s provider-managed auth flow and precise redirect behavior. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/blocks/signup-form.

The source/doc describes personal 2FA, password and active-session management. It cannot replace independent security event history, compromise review or bootstrap authority. It is already narrowly adapted around live Clerk content on the Account security route. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/blocks/security-settings.

Its actual hierarchy is an unread notification inbox with expandable/read/dismiss items and keeps its own notification copy after mount; it is not preference settings. Current switches apply a typed preference patch with expectedRevision. Upstream source: Arc upstream notification-center/notification-center.tsx:108.

This block edits a permission matrix with simulated inline role/group/grant state; current TeamRolesPage assigns workspace roles to people. Its own docs say to use team-members to assign roles to people. Upstream source: Arc upstream roles-permissions/roles-permissions.tsx:32.

This block owns a single scrolling form, draft baseline, unsaved-change bar and one save callback. Upstream docs say use settings-page for short paged profile forms and avoid settings-command for a single form. Current routes separate Clerk/account, tax, spend, key issuance, receipts and authority-sensitive actions, each with distinct persistence/results. Upstream source: Arc upstream settings-command/settings-command.tsx:289.

The source/docs target release notes grouped by month, with release-type filters and subscribe behavior. Security-history rows carry observed/recorded time, source, actor/target and correlation references under cursor paging; this is not a release feed. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/blocks/changelog-feed.

The source/docs use local user-toggleable checks to unlock a release action. Compromise review and decommission fences are authoritative external conditions; turning them into local checkboxes could imply recovery or close eligibility that the source has not confirmed. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/blocks/release-readiness.

The source/docs implement subscription cancellation with retention offers, discount/pause states and sample prices. Workspace close and ownership transfer use owner-only authority, decommission fences, typed name/successor and separate confirmation; the commercial action is different. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/blocks/cancel-flow.

This generic wizard supplies Back/Continue/progress/success state; it does not replace privacy-correction validation/receipt semantics, tax validation, or bootstrap operation/readback/idempotency. Adapting its structure would be a deliberate flow redesign, not a direct presenter replacement. Upstream docs: https://uiarc.dev/components/multi-step-form.

This is a component rather than a full block. AeRecordTable is already an Arc-derived sortable table adaptation; the security table adds AE evidence renderers and a separate cursor-paging/retry region. Replacing only the table component is at most a moderate region migration and risks filter/focus contracts.

Its diff approval and run timeline demo states cannot stand in for Quote/Call authority, Clerk reverification, or AE approval/refusal callbacks.
The Tool review submits one schema-defined input object and keeps a JSON fallback; a guided wizard changes the external form contract.
Add-credit is prepaid funding with exact balance, payment-confirmation and resume state, not a wallet action or buyer purchase checkout.

market.reason: Upstream is a Pro shop with local price/color/size/stock filters, sorting and quick-add/cart state; its own guidance rejects huge faceted server-search catalogs. The live AE route already retains adapted media/quick-action/card structure while keeping server search, cursor and save/compare handlers outside it.

Upstream expects finish/size variants, reviews, shipping and add-to-cart/restock behavior. The live AE adapter already retains the gallery/decision/detail hierarchy while its facts, Quote/Call readiness, source distinction and exact action remain AE-owned.

Upstream has one highlighted product and one CTA. DirectoryComparison needs independent inspect links for each Tool and source-aware unpublished values; its current Arc-derived table already preserves that custom contract.
The upstream block owns local query filtering and selection; it cannot directly retain AE’s server async search, controlled selection guards, IME handling, saved-need state and cursor continuation.
This is a tradable-instrument terminal with candlesticks, OHLC, watchlists and orders. Tool marketplace records are service supply, not financial assets.

money-and-activity.reason: A moderate table-region fit for ActivityCallQueue, not a full-block replacement. Its current source has no per-column comparator prop, while AE amount sorting explicitly uses BigInt; it also does not own the surrounding queue hierarchy.

The activity route supplies period totals and paged rows, not the dailyCall series required by the adapted block. It cannot replace ActivityMonthlySummary without adding daily source data or drawing an empty/fabricated chart.

Arc Timeline requires actual event timestamps, groups newest-first by day, and represents activity events; CallReceiptStageView has ordered status facts without per-stage times and can contain non-monotonic complete/attention states.

Stepper's current index implies prior steps are complete and later steps are not started; recorded receipt stages can have attention or completion across otherwise pending stages, so one index would misstate status.

The upstream whole AgentRun is a live scripted workflow with approval, retry, and result behavior. Only the installed controlled ArcAgentRunTimeline subregion is a moderate candidate for the static receipt stage list.
The block is a usage/plan/forecast/alerts/invoice dashboard. These Calls and prepaid credit records do not establish subscription plans, projections, alert rules, or invoice state.

The adapted BillingOverview balance/funding block is already live under Credit. Its BillingHistory region wraps AE AccountHistory; counting that wrapper as a new replacement would overstate Arc adoption.

The sample wallet card presents send/deposit/swap/buy actions and local balances/history, while AE credit is server-authoritative prepaid funding with separate purchased/promotional balances and a secure checkout.
The block presents a checkout with promo, tax, and pay controls; Call receipts are post-purchase records and must not acquire new payment actions or inferred purchase semantics.

operator.reason: Marketplace metrics returns only the selected 7/30/90-day window and no breakdown data; the block needs two periods and breakdowns.
AE readiness is read-only verified evidence with expiry, not a local checklist or launch action.
Provider records and connections are not a simulated third-party OAuth directory with connect/disconnect actions.
AE Calls and admin commands have commercial authority, payment uncertainty and receipt semantics; agent-run sample approval is not a substitute.
The exact adapted block is already in AdminMetricsPage; its generated analytics/source data must not be used for overview or treasury.
Treasury balance, reconciliation and payment controls are not a trading venue or candlestick series.

provider.reason: Actual source is a storefront with price/color/size/stock filters, photo cards and quick-add cart state; neither Provider Tool proof nor owner inventory has retail variants or purchase actions. Verified upstream source and When-not-to-use.

Useful only as a table component region, not a full block; its documented API has no controlled global filter or caller-provided row continuation, and current inventory also needs compact cards and cursor paging.

The six-cell block renders interactive sample product UI; replacing it with current four ordered supply steps would require custom visuals and change sequence, so it is not a direct fit. Verified upstream source.
Its described plan picker, usage, invoices and card surface would invent subscription/billing UI around Call obligations and recorded transfers.
Its live run, tool-call and approval-diff states do not represent source checks, provider lifecycle, readiness or offboarding.
Its promo, discount, tax and pay states are checkout behavior; the price revision modal computes and publishes a new Tool revision.

public-and-support.reason: Pro source is a fixed Halden demo with sample APIs, authors, versions and local navigation state; it has no dynamic document-content API.
The current status route contains health probes, not traffic KPIs or charts; this block would invent metrics.
Its Connect/Connected controls describe OAuth app connections, not observed website, API and catalogue health.
It introduces a validated form and completion state; no support-thread or contact submission transport exists.
It is a message-thread UI; support currently exposes mailto, public issues and safe Call references only.
Its six cells use miniature product UIs; the About presenter has four literal responsibility statements.
AeSiteCtaBand description is rich content with clickable ABN and email links; the block accepts a string.
It can replace only the JSON preformatted frame; it cannot replace the async confirmation dialog and its explicit-copy guard.
AeSiteNav is an auth-gated primary-nav fragment; SiteHeader adds an unrelated marketing header and mobile menu state.
Arc sample sign-in is not Clerk identity authority; current panel preserves Clerk content and focus semantics.

shared.reason: Its actual source owns sample workspaces, favorites, search and inline project creation; docs say use sidebar-rail when a full app shell needs a mobile sheet. AE route navigation is already supplied to SidebarRail.

Its source exports a no-props four-scene gallery with fictional search/offline/inbox/404 copy and simulated actions; docs recommend extracting a scene or using the empty-state component for a simple caller-owned state.
